digest.intro: Three nuclear powers meet in Shenzhen; physics, fabrication, and brains all crack open.

items.title: Xi, Trump, and Putin Sit Down in Shenzhen
items.blurb: China's Foreign Ministry confirmed the trilateral meeting on the sidelines of APEC — the first time all three leaders have been in the same room. Ukraine may not even be on the formal agenda, which is itself the story: a war-shaping negotiation happening entirely on Xi's terms, in Xi's city. Meanwhile, Zelenskyy says renewed Starshield restrictions are letting Russian drones reach Ukrainian infrastructure unimpeded — the battlefield and the summit are connected.

items.title: Ukraine Destroyed the Kerch Bridge Using an Airborne Mesh Radio Network
items.blurb: On the nights of November 15–16, Ukrainian drones overwhelmed Russian air defenses while a flying mesh of relay nodes — each drone acting as a signal repeater — let operators 250 km away guide the Flamingo cruise missile into the bridge's weakest structural points, collapsing one of two steel arches. The technique is a direct adaptation of a Russian innovation, turned back on them. The fact that it worked without Starlink is the pointed message.

items.title: Trump Is Weighing a Strike on Iran
items.blurb: U.S. and Israeli officials told the NYT that Trump is actively weighing a strike after intelligence about a potential Iranian dirty bomb, with Israel pushing for speed. A Houthi missile visibly damaged the Public Investment Fund Tower in Riyadh today — the Iran war is now touching Saudi Arabia's most symbolic financial real estate. Trump's January 1 deadline comment remains unexplained.

items.title: Claude Solved Two Open Problems in Black Hole Physics
items.blurb: These aren't benchmark wins — Anthropic is claiming Claude completed a holographic duality calculation that physicists set up 20 years ago and never finished, and separately found the exact limit of a technique used to test quantum gravity candidates. Both results are out as preprints. The significance isn't just the answers; it's that an AI navigated genuine open-ended theoretical physics, not a closed problem with a known solution waiting to be matched.

items.title: Fat-Derived Stem Cells Injected Directly Into Alzheimer's Brains — First Human Trial
items.blurb: In a six-patient Phase 1 trial, Dr. Christopher Duma's team at Hoag drew stem cells from patients' own body fat and injected them into the brain — not to clear amyloid plaques like existing drugs, but to interrupt multiple destructive processes simultaneously. Five of six showed cognitive improvement and reduced amyloid on scans; spinal fluid markers also improved. The honest caveat: gains weren't sustained over the full year, and six patients proves nothing — but the safety signal and mechanism are genuinely new.

items.title: A Human Liver Kept Alive Outside the Body for Seven Weeks
items.blurb: Carlo Pulitano's team in Sydney connected a donated liver to what he calls an "artificial body" — automated pumps, sensors, nutrient delivery, waste removal — and kept it at full body temperature (37°C) for seven weeks. The previous record, set in Switzerland, was two weeks. Most transplant organs currently survive only hours in ice; this threatens to make organ banking, not just transport, a realistic category.

items.title: Fanzines.app: 8-Page Booklets from a Single Sheet, Laid Out in the Browser
items.blurb: The fold is old — one A4, three folds, one cut, eight pages, no glue — but the layout problem was always annoying: the top row of panels has to be rotated 180° and the page order is non-obvious. This browser tool handles all of that, lets you place photos and text right-side up, and exports a 300 DPI print-ready PDF with nothing uploaded to a server. It's a very small thing that removes the last friction between having something to say and handing it to someone physically.

items.title: Wunderkammer: How Curiosity Cabinets Became the First Museums
items.blurb: The Nerdwriter — one of the more careful video essayists working — made this for the National Gallery of Art: the Wunderkammer as a 16th-century response to information overload, when global trade made the world suddenly too large to mentally hold. Nautilus shells, automata, taxidermied exotica, forged unicorn horns — all crammed together as a way of saying: *the world is bigger than our categories*. The parallel to now is not subtle, and he doesn't force it.

facts.fact: Ukrainian operators guided missiles into the Kerch Bridge from over 250 kilometers away using a mesh of relay drones as a makeshift communications network — no military Starlink required.
The previous record for keeping a human organ alive outside the body was roughly two weeks; Australian surgeons just held a liver at full body temperature for seven weeks.
Claude completed a black hole physics calculation that was set up by physicists more than 20 years ago and had never been solved — the result is now out as a preprint.
In the Alzheimer's stem cell trial, the cells were drawn from each patient's own body fat — not a donor — and injected directly into the brain in a single session.

The Trump–Xi–Putin meeting in Shenzhen is happening on the sidelines of APEC, with Ukraine potentially not even on the formal agenda — meaning the war's biggest diplomatic moment may produce no official record.

art_picks.title: Sans Soleil
art_picks.creator: Chris Marker
art_picks.why: A film that works as pure systems theory disguised as a travel essay — Marker traces the invisible codes running Japan and Guinea-Bissau through images, memory, and ritual, asking how societies construct meaning from time. It's the kind of movie that rewires how you look at everything afterward.

art_picks.title: Mycelium Networks / Process works
art_picks.creator: Semiconductor (Ruth Jarman & Joe Gerhardt)
art_picks.why: Semiconductor makes A/V installations from raw scientific data — geomagnetic fields, particle physics, seismic activity — rendering the invisible forces that shape matter into something you feel bodily. The edge between measurement and sensation, nature as software.

art_picks.title: Selected Ambient Works Volume II
art_picks.creator: Aphex Twin
art_picks.why: One of the few records that genuinely operates as architecture — untitled, mostly beatless, structured entirely around texture and space. It's less listened-to than inhabited, and it rewards the kind of obsessive, pattern-seeking attention Willem applies to systems.

events.name: James Turrell: Something Old, Something New, Something Borrowed, Something Blue
events.venue: Almine Rech New York — 39 E 78th St, Upper East Side
events.why: Fifteen-plus works including a new Shallow Space and new Glassworks — Turrell remains the definitive artist of perception-as-medium, and a dedicated show of new pieces is rare enough to warrant the uptown trip.

events.name: Na Mira: NO SMOKING
events.venue: MoMA, Kravis Studio, Floor 4 — 11 W 53rd St, Manhattan
events.why: A newly commissioned media installation drawing on Korean shamanism, structural filmmaking, fûkeiron landscape theory, and footage shot inside a military cinema on a US-Mexico border base — using radio frequencies, infrared, and holography to degrade the very imaging technologies the piece interrogates.

events.name: Addie Wagenknecht: Shelf Life
events.venue: Nguyen Wahed — 504 E 12th St, East Village
events.why: Wagenknecht blends hacker culture, surveillance systems, and hardware manipulation into work that sits squarely at the physical/digital seam Willem lives in — and Nguyen Wahed is one of the few NYC galleries with a genuine generative/digital-art program rather than a tokenistic one.

events.name: Leonora Carrington & Cecilia Vicuña
events.why: Opens today — a pairing of two artists whose practices fuse mythology, material systems, and self-made cosmologies: Carrington's surrealist-shamanist paintings alongside Vicuña's fiber/language works, both using aesthetic surfaces to encode deep structure.

events.name: Time Warp NYC 2026
events.venue: Duggal Greenhouse & Agger Building, Brooklyn Navy Yard
events.why: Two-night, two-warehouse industrial techno takeover with Sven Väth, DVS1, Âme, Anetha, and a real local contingent (Annie Lew, Kilopatrah Jones, KYRUH) — serious about production design and sound rather than spectacle, and the Brooklyn Navy Yard setting earns its own atmosphere.
